name: Colin Mensah

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m a senior researcher with the Work Futures Panel, an independent group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. This interview is confidential. Tell me about an ordinary day at work.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and manage the royalty settlements team inside a large book publisher. Eight people check sales reports, return allowances and the amounts owed to writers; I take the disputes where a contract’s wording and a warehouse return point in different directions. I’m good at finding which edition was actually sold, but I tire of telling a writer that a clean statement is not necessarily a correct one.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How did you get there, and what is the household picture?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I did an MBA after years in book distribution, and the company pays me well because I can trace a payment from a till to a contract. My wife Leila is a theatre lighting technician; our children are nine and fourteen, and we have a mortgage. We have about eleven months of expenses in cash and there are several publishers and distributors nearby. I use AI now and then to turn a dense statement into a draft explanation, but I check the underlying sales ledger first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell writers that the explanation may come faster, but their sales and returns still need a person who can point to a ledger line. A polished statement is not proof of a correct royalty.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My senior dispute work should still be needed, and eleven months saved gives us room if a theatre production ends early. I would not suddenly spend the reserve because AI disappointed the market.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next quarter I’d keep the monthly author-dispute desk and have each disputed return traced to its warehouse docket before signing a payment. In the first year Leila and I would continue putting 250 monthly into the children’s education account while both wages arrive.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about the job and our bills in this picture. The cash buffer lets me keep treating a disputed author payment carefully.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which return would you check first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A writer’s statement once showed sixty returned copies from a shop that had never carried that writer’s edition. The warehouse code was for a different cover, and a neat statement hid it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why the education account rather than more holidays?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our older child will be choosing a course soon. I can enjoy a holiday after the writer is paid and our children’s fees are covered.

say: I’d trace **warehouse returns** before signing a writer’s royalty payment.
A faster explanation does not prove the **sales ledger** is right.
think: My **dispute role** should remain useful in a plateau.
Eleven months cash protects us if Leila’s **theatre contract** ends early.
do: Keep the **monthly author desk** and check each disputed return against its warehouse docket.
Continue **250 monthly** to the children’s education account while both wages arrive.
feel: I feel **calm** about work and household bills.
S0.quote: A writer’s statement once showed sixty returned copies from a shop that had never carried that writer’s edition.
fieldNote: His MBA is backed by **distribution knowledge** and a high salary.
He holds **eleven months cash**, beyond ordinary emergency savings.
He uses AI **occasionally** for explanations, not ledger approval.

steps.text: Trace disputed author returns to warehouse dockets before approving royalty payments
Continue 250 monthly education-account transfer while both wages arrive

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say reconciliation software could find a wrong return much faster, provided writers can challenge the record. I would keep a named editor or accountant available when the code and the physical book disagree.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A machine may do the first pass of most of our eight jobs, leaving two people for exceptions. I might remain to settle hard cases, but even a trusted manager can lose a post if the whole desk merges with another.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In December I’d ask our audit head to test the tool on one prior print run with written author consent and compare its return list with the physical dockets. If the author and audit head both accept the findings, I’d use it for that run in the first year and ask for a written plan for the clerks whose checks disappear.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious about the eight people and about my own post. A correct calculation still has a person at the other end of the payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why ask the author for consent on an old run?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The contract lets us inspect returns, but I will not put an unpublished sales history into a vendor tool without permission. The writer has to know what is being tested.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell the two who might remain?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: There is no list yet. I would not promise a colleague a job on the strength of my guess about how the company will merge desks.

say: I’d demand **author consent** before using a vendor tool on unpublished sales history.
A writer needs a **named human contact** when return codes and physical books disagree.
think: AI may leave **two exception workers** from eight.
My skill might retain me, but a desk merger could remove **my manager post**.
do: Ask the **audit head** to compare one consented print run with physical dockets.
Use the tool only after **author and audit approval**, then seek a written staffing plan.
feel: I feel **anxious** about colleagues and my own post.
S1.quote: I would not promise a colleague a job on the strength of my guess about how the company will merge desks.
fieldNote: He requires **writer consent** before using a vendor system.
His trial depends on **two approvals** and a physical record check.
He does not claim his expertise guarantees **manager headcount**.

steps.text: Ask audit head to test one prior print run only with written author consent
Use tool for that run only after author and audit head accept physical-docket findings

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell writers to download their contracts and payment histories and demand a real appeal address. The company should give staff a date and written terms before closing any desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 could read contracts, match returns and answer writers more cheaply than I can, so I expect my settlements post to end. Leila’s physical lighting rig work may carry on until robots around 2031, but her theatre contracts alone would not cover our mortgage and both children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I’d keep the eleven-month reserve liquid and ask HR for the exact notice and severance terms, without budgeting for severance until confirmed. Before 2028 I’d ask two local distributors about paid contract-dispute openings; in the first year after AGI, I’d accept a posted role only if its written pay plus Leila’s actual bookings cover the mortgage and family bills, and I would treat it as temporary thinking work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m alarmed by the prospect of my salary ending, though we have time in the bank. Eleven months is a runway, not a new profession.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say to your children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell them our bills can be paid for a while, but the next school trip waits until we know my wage. I will not tell them the cash is endless.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why look at another distributor if AGI can settle contracts?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A firm may still pay someone to handle a writer’s challenge for a time. Another settlement desk is a paid bridge, not shelter from 2028 AGI.

say: I’d tell writers to keep **contracts and payment histories** and ask for a reachable appeal address.
Staff deserve **written closure terms** before the settlements desk shuts.
think: I expect my **settlements post to end** with 2028 AGI.
Leila’s physical rig work may last until **2031 robots**, but bookings alone cannot cover our mortgage.
do: Keep **eleven months cash** liquid and request notice and severance terms without assuming payment.
Ask about **paid distributor openings** before 2028; accept afterward only if written pay plus Leila’s bookings cover family bills.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about losing the higher wage.
S2.quote: Eleven months is a runway, not a new profession.
fieldNote: His eleven-month buffer gives **search time**, not AGI immunity.
A second contract desk remains **thinking work** exposed at 2028.
An offer must combine **written pay** with Leila’s actual bookings to cover family bills.

steps.text: Keep eleven-month reserve liquid and request written notice and severance terms
Ask two local distributors about paid dispute openings before 2028
Accept posted dispute role after 2028 only if written pay plus Leila’s bookings cover family bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say five years gives publishers time to settle disputed back payments and show staff a real timetable. I would want authors to know who can still hear a challenge after the ledger is automated.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could reduce the mortgage while my salary and Leila’s bookings hold, but the settlement desk could still close in 2031. Physical warehouse returns work may last until robots around 2034, yet its schedules and accounting face AGI in 2031 too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From January 2027 I’d overpay the mortgage by 300 a month only after our eleven-month reserve and the children’s education money remain intact. Before 2031 I’d seek a written offer from a local publisher for paid author-dispute work if it covers our mortgage and bills; after AGI I’d take it only while the publisher actually pays for human appeals, knowing the new title does not remove AGI exposure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious but more deliberate than in the two-year picture. I can compare contracts and reduce debt without gambling the children’s fund.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move into warehouse work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I know the dockets, but I do not pretend I can run a warehouse shift tomorrow. I would need a posted paid opening and practical training before counting it as income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if Leila’s bookings slip?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then the extra 300 stops first. I would rather keep the eleven months cash than brag about how fast the mortgage shrank.

say: I’d demand a **real closure timetable** and settle disputed back payments.
Authors need a **named appeal contact** after the ledger changes.
think: Mortgage reduction depends on **both incomes** continuing.
Warehouse schedules face **2031 AGI** before physical returns face 2034 robots.
do: Overpay **300 monthly** only while both wages hold and the reserve and children’s education account remain intact.
Seek **written local publisher work** before 2031 at mortgage-and-bills-covering pay.
Take **paid human appeals** after 2031 only while the new publisher funds them.
feel: I feel **anxious** but able to compare contracts.
S3.quote: I would rather keep the eleven months cash than brag about how fast the mortgage shrank.
fieldNote: He prefers debt reduction without spending the **education account**.
A local appeals post is **exposed thinking work**, even if humans are retained temporarily.
He declines to claim **warehouse competence** without paid opening and training.

steps.text: Overpay mortgage 300 monthly only while both incomes hold and reserve and education account remain intact
Seek written author-dispute offer before 2031 only with mortgage-and-bills-covering pay
Take human appeals after 2031 only while new publisher funds paid posts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say a decade allows a publisher to show staff what happens to royalties and appeal staffing before the last week. I would urge writers to keep their own sales records, whatever system we use.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’ll be 53 in 2036, with the children nineteen and twenty-four. If our two wages last long enough, the mortgage could be small and the pension larger, but my royalty decisions still face 2036 AGI; warehouse schedules change then and physical handling follows robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next year I’d ask the pension provider for a written projection of what I could actually access at 53 and the net monthly income then, and compare it with the mortgage each birthday while keeping our eleven-month reserve. I’d consider leaving full-time work at 53 only if accessible pension income or a separately funded bridge covers our household and children’s costs, the mortgage is clear and Leila agrees. In the first year after AGI I’d keep paid author-dispute work if offered; if the age-53 money is unavailable or insufficient, I would continue seeking paid work instead of retiring.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m uneasy rather than frightened by the longer runway, provided the figures work. I would not call a wish to retire a pension.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the pension estimate falls short?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the pension is inaccessible or insufficient at 53, I keep looking for paid work and do not leave. I will not ask Leila to carry a mortgage because I liked a round number on a forecast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the children still be dependent?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Maybe in different ways, but I cannot write them out of the budget now. I would ask what each needs before treating a mortgage-free house as permission to stop earning.

say: I’d ask publishers for **advance appeal staffing plans** rather than a last-week notice.
Writers should keep **their own sales records** across any system change.
think: At **53 in 2036**, a smaller mortgage and larger pension are conditional on both wages.
Royalty decisions face **2036 AGI** before 2039 physical warehouse robots.
do: Request a **written age-53 pension projection** showing accessible funds and net income; compare it with the mortgage.
Consider **retirement at 53** only with accessible income or funded bridge, cleared mortgage, Leila’s agreement and covered family costs.
Keep **paid author appeals** after 2036 if offered; if age-53 income fails, seek paid work and do not retire.
feel: I feel **uneasy** but can use the decade to plan.
S4.quote: I would not call a wish to retire a pension.
fieldNote: His retirement option depends on **written pension numbers**, not current cash alone.
He requires **Leila’s agreement** and a cleared mortgage before leaving full-time work.
He knows royalty thinking work faces **2036 AGI**, while physical warehouse work follows later.

steps.text: Request written pension provider projection of age-53 access and net income
Consider retiring at 53 with accessible pension/funded bridge covering family costs cleared mortgage and Leila’s consent
Keep paid author-dispute work after 2036 only if publisher offers it
Seek paid work if age-53 income is unavailable or insufficient and defer retirement

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because I expect my settlements salary to end before the mortgage is small. Eleven months of cash helps us ask better questions, but it does not pay for decades. A written notice date, actual paid openings and an appeal line for writers would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask whether a writer trusts a royalty number that nobody at the publisher can explain. The amount on the statement is only half the promise. Someone at the publisher has to show a writer which book sales and returns produced the royalty payment.

headlineQuote: Someone at the publisher has to show a writer which book sales and returns produced the royalty payment.
portrait: **Colin**, 43, leads eight royalty settlement staff at a large book publisher.
His MBA, high pay and **eleven-month reserve** give his family room to choose.
Leila’s **theatre lighting bookings** are physical work but do not replace his salary.
He will try AI **with author consent** and audit evidence, while acknowledging his own post may go.
He treats early retirement as a **conditional calculation**, not a claim that savings already suffice.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end his settlements salary while the mortgage remains substantial.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, actual paid openings and an author appeal line would make decisions possible.
